beats.text: In a crash, time slows down. Right?
Researchers dropped volunteers about thirty meters into a net. Free fall.
Afterwards, they guessed their own fall had lasted about a third longer than other people's.
But during the fall, they watched a display flashing numbers too fast to read. If time really slowed, they could read them.
Fear makes memory record more detail. And more memory feels like more time.

sources: Stetson, Fiesta & Eagleman (2007). Does time really slow down during a frightening event? PLoS ONE 2(12). 31 m free fall into a net; participants estimated their own fall 36% longer than others'; could not read a perceptual chronometer at speeds above normal threshold. Via ScienceDaily.
